legend.type: BAU = business-as-usual (expected variation), BLACK-SWAN = rare high-impact event
legend.likelihood: Low / Medium / High — qualitative; where an official probability exists it is quoted with its source
legend.impact: Direction of impact on property value or personal wealth if the risk realizes
legend.affects: Which of the four decision strategies the risk changes: HOLD, SELL, EXCHANGE (sell + IRC 1031), ALL

risks.risk: Tenant same-store sales keep declining
risks.impact: Negative: weaker renewals, lower rent capacity
risks.evidence: FY2026 Q3 system SSS -1.1%; FY2026 guidance a low single-digit decline
risks.mitigation: Renewal with escalations; credit review; sell trigger on second consecutive year of decline

risks.risk: Tenant system keeps shrinking (elevated closures)
risks.impact: Negative: vacant-restaurant risk at or before expiry
risks.evidence: Q3 FY2026: 4 openings vs 17 closures; FY2026 guidance ~50-60 closures; management expects elevated closures into 2028 (earnings call, not a filing — see irregularity X-03)
risks.mitigation: Confirm assignment/sublease terms; size the reserve for re-tenanting; prefer selling before expiry if renewal terms are weak

risks.risk: Franchisee financial stress (bad debt, margin compression)
risks.impact: Negative: royalty/rent arrears flow-through to landlord credit
risks.evidence: Franchise-level margin fell to $60.3M from $66.2M with higher bad-debt expense; restaurant-level margin 17.6% vs 17.9%
risks.mitigation: Monitor tenant 10-Qs; require escrow/guaranty where negotiable

risks.risk: Exit cap-rate expansion compresses sale price
risks.impact: Negative
risks.evidence: 10-yr Treasury at 4.86% (2026-11-06) after moving between 4.84% and 4.95% in one week
risks.mitigation: Set a disciplined reserve price; stage the sale process; use the model's break-even cap grid

risks.risk: Measure ULA transfer tax raises the cost of any City of LA sale
risks.impact: Negative: 4.45% all-in on tier-1 consideration (City base + ULA)
risks.evidence: 4% ULA over $5.4M plus 0.45% base = 4.45%; tier 2 = 5.95% all-in
risks.mitigation: Test §1031 (defers gain but NOT transfer tax — see X-04); confirm parcel is inside City limits; model both with-ULA and without-ULA cases

risks.risk: ULA thresholds or rates change by ordinance or future ballot
risks.impact: Either direction
risks.evidence: Thresholds adjust every July 1 via BLS chained CPI; rates fixed by ordinance 187692 unless amended
risks.mitigation: Check thresholds at closing date; treat ULA as permanent in base case

risks.risk: Buyer's Prop 13 reassessment raises the buyer's tax bill and lowers their bid
risks.impact: Negative: effective buyer yield required rises
risks.evidence: Change of ownership resets base year value to purchase price; levy then up to 1% plus voter-approved debt
risks.mitigation: Model the buyer's after-tax yield, not just the headline cap rate

risks.risk: County population decline erodes long-run retail/restaurant demand
risks.impact: Negative structural headwind to rent and occupancy by 2030-2035
risks.evidence: LA County population -3.2% 2020-2025 (Census V2025); DOF -0.6% in the year to 2026-01-01
risks.mitigation: Weight renewal probability lower; prefer shorter exit paths when bids are near fair value

risks.risk: School enrollment collapse reduces household formation in the trade area
risks.impact: Negative long-run demand signal
risks.evidence: DOF projects LA County K-12 enrollment down 240,800 students by 2035-36
risks.mitigation: Treat as a discount on the 2032-2035 leg of any hold case

risks.risk: Wage inflation compresses restaurant operating margins
risks.impact: Negative: pressure on tenant margins and renewals
risks.evidence: City minimum wage $18.42/hr from 2026-07-01; state $16.90; fast-food chains $20.00; ECI metro +3.9% YoY
risks.mitigation: Price escalations above wage inflation in any renewal

risks.risk: Food and energy price spikes
risks.impact: Negative: tenant margins, then rents
risks.evidence: Metro CPI food +2.8% and energy +20.3% YoY in Sep 2026
risks.mitigation: CPI-linked escalators in the renewed lease

risks.risk: Local job losses in information/finance offset gains elsewhere
risks.impact: Mixed: county unemployment still falling but sectoral weakness persists
risks.evidence: Information -10,200 jobs YoY; financial activities -4,000; professional & business -3,500, while edu/health +37,500
risks.mitigation: Track monthly EDD releases as a trigger series

risks.risk: Interest rates rise further (UCLA Anderson expects a December 2026 hike)
risks.impact: Negative for cap rates, positive for reinvestment yield
risks.evidence: Forecast: +25 bp in December 2026 after the September hike to 3.75%-4.00%
risks.mitigation: Fix replacement financing early; use the DGS10-anchored reinvestment assumption in the model

risks.risk: Renewal negotiated with below-market rent
risks.impact: Negative: locked-in income shortfall for the option period
risks.evidence: Qualitative; no official source exists for a private negotiation
risks.mitigation: Pre-negotiate escalators; compare against the official6.8% net-lease benchmark before accepting

risks.risk: Vacancy and re-tenanting time at expiry
risks.impact: Negative: downtime plus TI/LC at 2030-2035 expiry
risks.evidence: Benchmark portfolio occupancy 98.8% with 8.5-yr WALT shows best-in-class landlords still carry vacancy; a single-asset restaurant carries idiosyncratic vacancy risk
risks.mitigation: Start renewal talks 24-36 months before expiry; keep a re-tenanting reserve

risks.risk: Securitization/tenant refinancing events
risks.impact: Indirect: tenant credit moves with financing markets
risks.evidence: Tenant issued $500M of 2026-1 Class A-2 Notes (repayment May 2031) and prepaid $110M in Q3 FY2026
risks.mitigation: Calendar the May 2031 maturity against the 2030-2035 expiry window

risks.risk: Major earthquake in the Los Angeles region
risks.impact: Severe: structural damage, business interruption, demand shock
risks.evidence: USGS UCERF3: 60% M6.7+, 46% M7.0+, 31% M7.5+ within 30 years
risks.mitigation: Verify earthquake coverage (standard policies exclude it); diversified §1031 proceeds survive a single-asset loss

risks.risk: Wildfire event of Eaton/Palisades scale
risks.likelihood: Low-Medium per parcel; realized twice in Jan 2025
risks.impact: Severe in the wildland interface; indirect (insurance, demand) city-wide
risks.evidence: Eaton: 9,419 structures destroyed; Palisades: 6,845; both January 2025
risks.mitigation: Parcel-level check required (blank in this workbook, flag F-11); insurance market stress is the transmission channel

risks.risk: Insurance market shock (FAIR Plan assessment, premium spikes, non-renewals)
risks.impact: Negative: operating costs up, buyer pool down, values down
risks.evidence: $1B FAIR Plan assessment approved 2025-02-11, first in 30+ years; insurers may recoup 50%
risks.mitigation: Get bound quotes before listing; treat insurance as a first-order underwriting item

risks.risk: Tenant bankruptcy or abrupt brand failure
risks.impact: Severe: full rollover, re-tenanting at market cap
risks.evidence: Dividend suspended, guidance cut to low-single-digit SSS decline, elevated closures, refinancing completed May 2031 maturity
risks.mitigation: Diversification via §1031 into multi-tenant NNN; sell before expiry if credit deteriorates

risks.risk: National recession
risks.impact: Negative: rents, cap rates, tenant traffic
risks.evidence: Forecast notes risks from AI-equity correction and Middle East oil shock; California 'employment recession' continuing through 2026
risks.mitigation: Prefer strategies that preserve liquidity; avoid leverage

risks.risk: AI-equity correction or financing shock
risks.impact: Negative: wealth effect, cap-rate volatility
risks.evidence: Explicit downside risk named in the September 2026 UCLA Anderson outlook
risks.mitigation: Diversified reinvestment path; staged execution

risks.risk: Middle East escalation / oil price spike
risks.impact: Negative: inflation, rates, consumer spending
risks.evidence: Named as the biggest threat in the September 2026 outlook after the Iran oil shock
risks.mitigation: Model both rate paths; keep the hold/ sell decision reversible via triggers

risks.risk: Trade-policy shock hitting Port cargo and logistics employment
risks.impact: Negative: logistics jobs and regional demand
risks.evidence: Port at record cargo (Sept 2026 record; +3% YTD) but releases repeatedly cite tariff uncertainty
risks.mitigation: Watch monthly port releases as a trigger series

risks.risk: Pandemic-class demand shock
risks.impact: Severe short-run: restaurant traffic collapses
risks.evidence: Qualitative historical precedent; no official probability exists
risks.mitigation: Same as R20/R21: diversify, avoid over-leverage

risks.risk: New local transfer or wealth tax adopted
risks.impact: Negative: higher exit friction
risks.evidence: Nov 2026 ballot: Prop 43 (limit local revenue measures) was REJECTED unofficially with 57.0% No — no new constraint on local transfer taxes; certification due 2026-12-11
risks.mitigation: Re-read SoS results after certification; monitor City Clerk filings

risks.risk: Wildfire-adjacent rebuild demand or conversely, a second firestorm in the metro
risks.impact: Two-sided: rebuild lifts some construction demand; a second metro fire would hit insurance and demand
risks.evidence: Palisades (23,448 acres) and Eaton (14,021 acres) both 100% contained by 2025-01-31; causes arson and electrical
risks.mitigation: Insurance and location diligence before any hold extension

risks.risk: IRC Section 1031 legislative repeal or tightening
risks.impact: Removes the exchange path; raises the cost of selling
risks.evidence: The rule currently defers gain (45/180-day framework); no enacted change verified as of 2026-11-10
risks.mitigation: Execute identification deadlines strictly; do not build the plan around a future-law assumption
